solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: A French horse stuck in turf — as one unprepared?

indicators.note: stuck in means lodged inside, so the horse letter is placed within the word for turf

blocks.note: un is the French for a
a sod is a piece of turf
H is slang shorthand for heroin, called horse

explanation.surface: A French horse is turned out on the grass, apparently not ready for anything.
explanation.walkthrough: Horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H. The question mark admits the definition is loose: a horse without shoes is not ready for the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Unshod means without shoes, so a horse in that state is not equipped for work, hence unprepared.

clue.text: Superior firm in history to the north by the sea?

definitions.text: to the north by the sea?

indicators.note: in places the firm's abbreviation inside the word for history

blocks.note: U means upper class, superior
the past is history
Co. is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A posh firm with a long history up north beside the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the old label for upper-class usage, hence superior.
explanation.definitionFit: Upcoast means further up the coast, and on a map up is north, so northward along the shore.

clue.text: Ship's spar gets spray? Not unknown

indicators.note: not unknown here means without the algebraic unknown, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: a spritz is a spray or squirt
Z is an unknown quantity in algebra

explanation.surface: A ship's spar gets drenched by spray, which is hardly unheard of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not unknown' reads as 'familiar', but it means minus the algebra letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprit is a small diagonal spar that extends a fore-and-aft sail on a boat.

clue.text: Arab cloth of excellent quality plunged into dye

indicators.note: plunged into means dipped inside, so the quality letters go within the word for dye

blocks.note: a hue is a colour or tint, which a dye gives
A1 means first-class, written AI
Q is an abbreviation for quality

explanation.surface: Fine Arabian fabric dipped in a vat of dye.
explanation.walkthrough: A1, first-class, is written AI in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: A haique, or haik, is a large wrapping of cloth worn as an outer garment by Arabs.

clue.text: Evil spirits parted right away after being summoned up

indicators.note: away means gone, so the abbreviation for right is taken out
in a down entry, up means reading from bottom to top, so the word is turned round

blocks.note: severed means parted or cut off
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Demons were split apart, having been conjured up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Summoned' suits the evil spirits, but it is just padding for 'up', the reversal signal in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A deev, or dev, is a demon or evil spirit in Persian mythology; the plural names several.

clue.text: Talk about having church coffee party

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the word for talk is read from its end

blocks.note: taken as written
CH is the standard abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: Chatting about the church coffee morning.
explanation.definitionFit: A klatch, as in kaffeeklatsch, is an informal social gathering for coffee and gossip.

clue.text: African bird, last to ascent to highest point

indicators.text: last to ascent to highest point
indicators.note: in a down entry the top is the start, so the final letter climbs to the front

blocks.note: a rook is a crow-family bird

explanation.surface: An African bird, the last to climb to the summit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ascent' is printed where 'ascend' is meant. Moving the last letter of ROOK to the top gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kroo, or Kru, are a West African people of Liberia, famed as seamen; an African is a member.

clue.text: Summon expert to tackle urban areas half falling apart

indicators.note: half means only part of the word is kept, its second half dropped
to tackle is to grapple with, so the expert's word wraps round the town letters

blocks.note: an ace is an expert
cities are urban areas
surface padding: it paints decaying inner cities and supplies no letters

explanation.surface: Call in a specialist to deal with crumbling inner cities.
explanation.walkthrough: The expert's word is split after its second letter to take the half-word in; 'falling apart' is decoration for the urban-decay picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Accite is an archaic verb meaning to summon or cite, as to court.

clue.text: Foremost in the European Union with added weight — a German?

indicators.note: foremost picks out the very first letter of the next word

blocks.note: the first letter of the
EU is the European Union
a ton is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: A German carries a lot of weight at the head of the European Union.
explanation.definitionFit: A Teuton was a member of an ancient Germanic tribe, and the word now means a German person.

clue.text: Conservative baddy losing head — one generating lots of heat?

indicators.note: losing head means the first letter of the word for baddy goes

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
a malefactor is a wrongdoer

explanation.surface: A disgraced Tory villain is ousted, causing a heated row.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lots of heat' suggests controversy, but the definition is literal: a heater.
explanation.definitionFit: A calefactor is a heating device, such as a stove, from Latin calefacere, to make warm.

clue.text: Dad, say, in amble with aged Poppy's family

indicators.note: in places one word inside the other, here a word for state sitting within a slow walk

blocks.note: pa is an informal word for father
to pace is to walk steadily, as in an amble
to aver is to state or declare
ae. abbreviates Latin aetatis, of age, used in dates on memorials

explanation.surface: An elderly father strolls about with a poppy, a sentimental picture.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma after 'Dad' splits the clue: 'say' is a verb in its own right, not 'for example'. The insertion goes after the first letter of the walking word.
explanation.definitionFit: Papaveraceae is the botanical family name of the poppies, from Latin papaver, poppy.

clue.text: Fish in the same place, given external supervision

indicators.note: given external means wrapped from outside, so the reference abbreviation sits inside the word for looking after

blocks.note: care is charge or supervision
ib., short for ibidem, means in the same place in a reference

explanation.surface: A fish kept where it was found, under watchful supervision.
explanation.walkthrough: IB comes from ibidem, the footnote word used when citing the same book again.
explanation.definitionFit: Caribe is another name for the piranha, a South American freshwater predator.

clue.text: Keeper of birds treasuring larks

indicators.note: larks are pranks and capers, so the letters fool about into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A birdkeeper cherishes his larks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Larks' wants to be the birds kept, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An austringer is a falconer who keeps and flies goshawks and other short-winged hawks.

clue.text: Mongrel dog tribes let loose

indicators.note: let loose means set free and running wild, so the letters scatter into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Tribes unleash a stray mutt.
explanation.definitionFit: Bitser is Australian slang for a mutt, a cross-breed made of bits of this and bits of that.

clue.text: Magical old sect group outside college

indicators.note: outside means around, so the words for old and sect group go round the college letter

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
C is a standard abbreviation for college
a cult is a sect or devoted group

explanation.surface: An ancient sect's magic circle meeting outside a college.
explanation.walkthrough: The college letter goes between the old letter and the sect word.
explanation.definitionFit: Occult describes supernatural or mystical arts, which is what magic is.

clue.text: Old boy I call "deficient", incidentally

indicators.note: deficient means lacking something, so the word for call loses its final letter

blocks.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
taken as written
to term is to name or call

explanation.surface: A former pupil confesses, as an aside, that he calls something deficient.
explanation.walkthrough: TERM drops its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Obiter is Latin for by the way, used in English as an adverb meaning in passing.

clue.text: Savvy, like student avoiding second drug

indicators.note: avoiding the second one means the later of two matching letters is left out

blocks.note: as means like, in comparisons
a tutee is a student taught by a tutor
E is slang for ecstasy

explanation.surface: A smart student, clever enough to steer clear of a second dose.
explanation.walkthrough: TUTEE has two Es; the drug is the second one, and it goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Savvy as an adjective means shrewd and quick-witted, a direct synonym of astute.

clue.text: Aid denied to oft-failed bats?

indicators.note: denied to means kept from, so these letters are taken away from the word that follows
bats means crazy, so the remaining letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written: the letters to be removed
taken as written

explanation.surface: Batsmen who keep failing get no help.
explanation.walkthrough: Strike the letters of 'aid' from 'oft-failed' and rearrange the rest. Read whole, the clue describes the reprieve itself: a batter who keeps edging the ball survives because the fielders fail to help the bowler.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a let-off is a reprieve, such as a dropped catch, that lets a batsman survive a chance.

clue.text: Trip went wrong out of Spain with a knight trapped

indicators.note: out of means the abbreviation for Spain is removed from the word
trapped means caught inside, so the article and knight go within

blocks.note: erred means went wrong
E is the international vehicle code for Spain
taken as written
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A journey through Spain goes awry, with a knight caught up in it.
explanation.walkthrough: The second E of ERRED is the one lost; A and N go into the gap.
explanation.definitionFit: An errand is a short trip to deliver or fetch something.

clue.text: Explorer back after troubled rest — it may give anxiety

indicators.note: troubled means disturbed, so the letters of the word beside it are stirred up
back means the explorer's name is read from its end

blocks.note: the letters of rest rearranged
James Clark Ross was a British polar explorer

explanation.surface: A polar explorer comes home after a disturbed night, which leaves him anxious.
explanation.walkthrough: The explorer is Ross, who gave his name to the Ross Sea and Ross Ice Shelf.
explanation.definitionFit: A stressor is any agent or situation that causes stress, which commonly shows itself as anxiety.

clue.text: Bathe, yes? Tricky without a supplier of water

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the letter a is taken out first
tricky means awkward and twisted, so the remaining letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written: the letter to remove

explanation.surface: Should I bathe? Awkward, with no one to bring the water.
explanation.definitionFit: A bheesty, or bhisti, is an Indian water-carrier who delivers water in a leather bag.

clue.text: Old lover with blemish — not one carrying on?

indicators.note: not one means minus the Roman numeral for one

blocks.note: an ex is a former partner
a taint is a blemish or stain
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A former partner with a stained reputation, but not one having an affair?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carrying on' tempts as having an affair, which suits the old lover; here it means continuing to exist.
explanation.definitionFit: Extant means still in existence, surviving, which is continuing or carrying on.

clue.text: Monk could be secluded, not the first or last

indicators.note: not the first or last means both end letters of the word are dropped
could be suggests one possible arrangement of the letters, so they are reordered

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A monk might well be living apart, though not the first or last to do so.
explanation.definitionFit: A Culdee was a member of an early Celtic monastic order in Ireland and Scotland.

clue.text: Settle in part of hospital, difficult separation with wife going

indicators.note: going means departing, so the letter for wife leaves its word

blocks.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department
a wrench is a painful parting
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: Someone settles into a hospital ward after a painful split, the wife having walked out.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrench is to establish firmly, dig in, which is to settle oneself solidly.

clue.text: Having three spiny bits or one in region of the body

indicators.note: in places the numeral letter inside the word for a bodily region

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a tract is a system or region, like the digestive tract

explanation.surface: A description of something with three prickles, or one lodged somewhere in the body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Or' joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Triact describes a sponge spicule with three rays, three pointed arms radiating from a centre.

clue.text: What could make most be driven to extremity once

indicators.note: what could make asks what the letters can be built into, so they are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A question of what could make most people be pushed to the edge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Once' marks the definition as an old word.
explanation.definitionFit: Embost is an old hunting word for a quarry run to exhaustion, foaming at the mouth, so driven to its limit.

clue.text: Match with time-wasting — not the position today

definitions.note: fixure is obsolete; 'not ... today' flags that

indicators.note: wasting time here means the abbreviation for time is lost from the word

blocks.note: a fixture is a scheduled match
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A football match spoiled by time-wasting, the team no longer holding their position.
explanation.walkthrough: Fixure is a Shakespearean word, so 'not today' marks it as no longer in use.
explanation.definitionFit: Fixure meant firmness or fixed stance, an old word for a set position, as in Troilus and Cressida.

clue.text: Like nerve perhaps being shown by artist friend

blocks.note: RA is a Royal Academician
a mate is a friend

explanation.surface: An artist's friend shows some nerve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nerve' reads as courage, but it is the anatomical structure, which branches.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramate means branched, and nerves branch out into finer fibres, hence the 'perhaps' for an example.

clue.text: A thing growing in the garden is stemmed

blocks.note: taken as written
a rose is a garden flower

explanation.surface: A garden plant has a stem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stemmed' looks like the rose's stalk, but it is the verb: came from.
explanation.definitionFit: To stem from something is to originate in it, and arose means came into being, originated.

clue.text: Part of insect gives different insect trouble swinging round

indicators.note: swinging round means turning to face the other way, so the word for trouble is read from its end

blocks.note: an ant is an insect, a different one from the first
to ail is to trouble

explanation.surface: Part of one insect causes trouble for another as it swings about.
explanation.definitionFit: The antlia is the sucking proboscis of butterflies and moths, a mouthpart of the insect.

clue.text: "Stars" would exclude one the equivalent of Mars

indicators.note: would exclude means leave out, so the letter for one is removed

blocks.note: Aries is a constellation, a group of stars
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A star chart would leave out the planet Mars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stars' is in quotation marks because it stands for one particular constellation.
explanation.definitionFit: Ares is the Greek god of war, the counterpart of the Roman god Mars.

clue.text: Aura round old tribe that is located in north Africa

definitions.text: that is located in north Africa

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the word for aura wraps the tribe name

blocks.note: an air is an aura or atmosphere
Gad was one of the twelve tribes of Israel

explanation.surface: An aura surrounds an ancient tribe living in north Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That is' looks like i.e., but here it is part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Agadir is a port city on the Atlantic coast of Morocco, in north Africa.

clue.text: Fusses when soldiers come in at entrance

indicators.note: come in means enter, so the soldiers' letters go inside the word for fusses

blocks.note: ados are fusses
OR is other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: People fuss when soldiers turn up at the door.
explanation.definitionFit: Adoors is an archaic adverb meaning at the door, which is the entrance of a house.

clue.text: Sees nice BEd student finally excited with final certificate

indicators.note: finally points to the very last letter of the word it follows
excited means agitated, so these letters are stirred into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
the last letter of student

explanation.surface: A trainee teacher with a BEd is thrilled to see the final certificate at last.
explanation.walkthrough: BEd is a Bachelor of Education degree; its capitals are camouflage, and only its letters matter.
explanation.definitionFit: A bene decessit is a leaving certificate of good conduct, Latin for he departed well, given at the end of a course.

clue.text: Workers' guilds not initially considered in business set-ups

indicators.note: not initially tells us to drop the first letter of the word that follows

blocks.note: the first letter of considered
cartels are associations of businesses

explanation.surface: Trade unions are not at first taken into account in the formation of companies.
explanation.walkthrough: The C comes from 'considered' and is taken out of CARTELS.
explanation.definitionFit: An artel was a Russian cooperative of workers or craftsmen, a type of guild.

clue.text: At once old bird comes to cathedral city

blocks.note: a tit is a small songbird
Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire

explanation.surface: A bird flies straight to a cathedral city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old' belongs with the definition, flagging an archaic word, though it looks like it qualifies the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Titely is an obsolete adverb meaning quickly or immediately, the same as at once.
